newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes planned Turkish ministerial visit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes planned Turkish ministerial visit.

text.p: The State Department said on Friday it welcomed the opportunity for wide-ranging economic and political talks with a high-level Turkish official due to visit the United States.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin last month invited Turkish State Minister Fehim Adak to visit and "we understand the invitation has been accepted," department spokesman John Dinger said. He said the United States was still working out Adak's itinerary and agenda.
"Certainly, we welcome the opportunity to discuss economic and political issues with State Minister Adak," he added.
The United States has been concerned about Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's visits to Iran and Libya, fearing he could be leading his NATO-member country away from the West.

The New York Times quoted Erbakan as saying he was sending Adak to the United States as an envoy with a pledge of friendship and assurances that Washington had "no reason to be afraid of anything we are doing."
